You are the implementing engineer for Atlas ERP, in '/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp' on branch feat/hr-payroll (dev merged; HR employees 10.1 + leave 10.2 + time 10.3 done). NO git commands. uv at ~/.local/bin/uv; run `cd backend && ~/.local/bin/uv run <cmd>`. PostgreSQL 16 at postgresql+asyncpg://atlas:atlas@localhost:55432/atlas (LOCAL — run the full pg suite). This is the FINAL Phase 10 task; it completes HR.

READ FIRST (binding): docs/research/s4hana-parity.md HCM (v1 = "simple gross→net payroll posting a journal, explicitly flagged as not jurisdiction-compliant"); docs/architecture.md D-011 (payroll posts to finance via the event bus — the cross-module write pattern), D-012/D-013/D-014/D-015 (money), D-022/D-025/D-007/D-029; the cross-module-write-via-event precedents: 6.4 procurement match→AP-bill (procurement publishes, finance/handlers posts) and 7.4 sales billing→AR-invoice. Then read the EXACT code:
- backend/app/modules/hr/ — constants.py, models/ (org/leave/time packages), schemas, service/ package, queries.py (get_employee, employees with base_salary — the MASKED compensation; the payroll run READS base_salary, which is fine internally — masking is a serialization concern, the service reads the column directly), router.py + sibling routers, __init__.py, the mounting.
- backend/app/modules/finance/handlers.py + finance/queries.py + finance/constants posting purposes (you ADD payroll posting purposes: 'salary_expense', 'net_pay_clearing' / 'wages_payable', 'tax_withholding_payable' — and a finance/handlers handler that posts the payroll journal from the HR payroll event; OR HR publishes and finance posts — mirror 6.4/7.4 exactly: HR publishes PayrollPosted, finance/handlers.create_payroll_journal posts it). Look at how finance/service journal posting works (the handler builds a journal via the finance posting service / journal create+post — NOT raw inserts).
- backend/app/modules/finance/service/journal.py (the create+post entrypoint the finance handler uses).
- backend/tests/modules/hr/{factories.py, conftest.py} + finance factories (accounts, posting defaults, open period).
Latest migration = 0039.

CRITICAL §5: HR must NOT import finance/service. The payroll run computes gross→net per employee and PUBLISHES a PayrollPosted event; finance/handlers.py posts the consolidated payroll journal in the same transaction. Verify HR imports only finance/queries + the event. Document D-055.

TASK — PLAN 10.4: simple gross→net payroll run posting a journal (flagged non-compliant). Build (extend hr):

1. hr/constants.py additions: PayrollRunStatus (DRAFT|POSTED|CANCELLED). Permissions hr.payroll.read/.manage/.post. Number sequence 'hr.payroll_run' (PAY-…). Doc type + docflow links payroll-run→finance-journal. Event key 'hr.payroll.posted'. Posting purposes to ADD in finance: 'salary_expense' (Dr gross), 'wages_payable' or 'net_pay_clearing' (Cr net pay owed to employees), 'payroll_tax_payable' (Cr withheld tax). A SIMPLE flat tax model: a configurable flat tax_rate_percent (per run or a per-tenant default) computes withholding = gross × rate; net = gross − withholding. Document that this is a SIMPLISTIC, NON-JURISDICTION-COMPLIANT model (no brackets, no social security, no deductions beyond a flat tax) — the parity scope explicitly flags this.
2. hr/models additions (models/payroll.py; re-export):
   - `PayrollRun` (`hr_payroll_runs`): DocumentMixin header; run_number, status, period_start / period_end (Date), pay_date (Date), tax_rate_percent (MoneyType/Numeric — the flat withholding rate for this run), total_gross / total_tax / total_net (MoneyType — maintained), employee_count (int), currency_code, journal_entry_id (nullable link to the posted journal), posted_at, notes. 
   - `PayrollRunLine` (`hr_payroll_run_lines`): UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin; payroll_run_id (composite tenant_fk), employee_id (composite tenant_fk), gross_amount (MoneyType — from the employee's base_salary prorated for the period, or the monthly salary; v1: gross = base_salary (assume base_salary is the per-period gross, e.g. monthly; document the proration assumption — simplest: base_salary IS the period gross, no proration), tax_amount (MoneyType = gross × rate), net_amount (MoneyType = gross − tax), cost_center_id (opaque — the employee's department cost center for the salary-expense allocation, nullable). UNIQUE(tenant, payroll_run_id, employee_id).
3. hr/schemas additions: Create/Update/Read/Filter for PayrollRun (+lines read), action PostPayroll.
4. hr/service additions (service/payroll.py + payroll_post.py if >400):
   - create_payroll_run(period_start, period_end, pay_date, tax_rate_percent, employee_ids=None|all-active) — DRAFT; for each active employee with a base_salary, compute a PayrollRunLine: gross = base_salary, tax = quantize(gross × tax_rate_percent/100), net = gross − tax; resolve the employee's cost center (department's cost_center_id, via hr — the employee/department carries it) for the expense allocation; sum totals; claim PAY number. (Employees without a base_salary are skipped or 0 — document.) 
   - post_payroll_run(run_id) — in run_in_uow: PUBLISH PayrollPosted carrying the per-line gross/tax/net + cost-center allocation + the posting accounts; finance/handlers.py posts ONE consolidated journal: Dr salary_expense (total gross, optionally split by cost center for CO), Cr payroll_tax_payable (total tax), Cr wages_payable/net_pay_clearing (total net) — balanced (gross = tax + net). Set the run POSTED, link journal_entry_id + docflow run→journal. Atomic; closed-period pay_date rolls back. Idempotent. cancel DRAFT-only.
   - The salary-expense Dr SHOULD carry the cost-center dimension per line (so CO cost-center reports include labor) — post per-(cost-center) salary-expense lines summing to total gross, OR one line if no cost centers; document.
5. finance: add the three posting purposes + finance/queries helpers + the finance/handlers.create_payroll_journal handler (registered in app.main). The handler builds the journal via the finance posting service.
6. hr/queries additions: get_payroll_run, payroll_runs_for_period, payroll_lines_for_run.
7. hr/router additions (payroll_router sibling, mounted): payroll-runs (CRUD + post + cancel; list paginated, filter period/status), GET /{id} (+lines). Permission-guard (manage vs post). PERFORMANCE §6. Mount.
8. hr/events.py (NEW — HR's first cross-module event): PayrollPosted. 
9. Migration 0040_hr_payroll.py (down_revision 0039): hr_payroll_runs + hr_payroll_run_lines + indexes. No trigger-bearing alters.
10. docs/modules/hr.md: add a Payroll section — THE NON-COMPLIANCE FLAG prominently (simplistic flat-tax gross→net, NOT jurisdiction-compliant, no brackets/social-security/deductions), the gross→net computation, the consolidated journal (Dr salary-expense by cost center / Cr tax-payable / Cr wages-payable), the event-bus posting, closed-period rollback. DECISIONS.md D-055 (payroll: flat-tax non-compliant gross→net; payroll run → consolidated finance journal via the event bus; salary expense carries cost-center dimension; base_salary = period gross assumption).
11. Tests: test_payroll.py (create computes gross/tax/net correctly per the flat rate, totals, skips no-salary employees, cost-center resolution), test_payroll_post.py (post → a balanced finance journal exists: Dr salary-expense / Cr tax-payable + Cr wages-payable, gross = tax + net, docflow run→journal, the salary expense carries the cost-center dimension; closed-period rollback; idempotent re-post rejected), test_payroll_api.py (endpoints + RBAC manage/post + pagination + ≤3 budgets + tenant isolation). HEED issue #53 (no same-session post-failure state assertions for handler-raised errors). The KEY test: the payroll journal balances (gross = tax + net) and posts to the right accounts via the event.

RULES: no TODO/stub/dead-file; absolute imports; ruff + pytest FULLY green SQLite (`-m "not pg and not perf"`) AND `-m pg` (reset pg schema, alembic upgrade head, run -m pg); delete stray atlas.db; every file <400 lines; comments only non-obvious; don't print file contents. Update PROGRESS.md + tick PLAN 10.4 (note Phase 10 / HR COMPLETE) + DECISIONS.md D-055. Run STRUCTURE §9 self-check (esp. §5 — HR→finance via event + queries only) and report it.

Return: files created/changed, the gross→net flat-tax model + the non-compliance flag, the payroll→journal event mechanism + §5 verification, the consolidated journal postings (+ cost-center dimension), the balancing invariant (gross = tax + net), test counts (SQLite total+new, pg), migration number, §9 self-check, deviations.

1	"""Finance domain-event handlers (D-011) — cross-module subscribers (PLAN 5.3 / 6.4).
2	
3	``post_stock_valuation_journal`` (PLAN 5.3, D-020) subscribes to ``inventory.stock.valued`` and
4	posts the COGS/inventory valuation journal in the SAME transaction as the stock move (D-011
5	run_in_uow drains before commit; D-020 same-transaction COGS). Because the handler shares the
6	session and any handler exception rolls the WHOLE transaction back, a stock move can never commit
7	without its journal entry, or vice versa — the load-bearing atomicity invariant. The journal posts
8	with the move's ``move_date``: a date in a CLOSED period makes the journal's period trigger fire
9	inside this same transaction, which rolls the whole move back (you cannot move stock into a closed
10	accounting period — correct by construction).
11	
12	``create_bill_for_match`` (PLAN 6.4, D-042) subscribes to ``procurement.invoice_match.matched`` and
13	creates + posts the AP vendor bill (Dr GR/IR at PO cost + Dr/Cr purchase-price-variance for the
14	in-tolerance price difference + Dr input tax / Cr AP control at the vendor-invoiced total) in the
15	SAME transaction as the match post. Procurement PUBLISHES the event; finance handles its OWN bill
16	posting (procurement must not import finance/service — STRUCTURE §5). The bill DEBITS GR/IR at
17	exactly the cost the goods receipt CREDITED it at receipt, so the GR/IR clearing account nets to
18	zero — the procure-to-pay loop closes. A closed invoice period trips the bill's journal period
19	trigger here and rolls the whole match post back.
20	
21	``post_production_variance`` (PLAN 8.2, D-048) subscribes to the manufacturing OrderFinished event
22	and posts the residual WIP-variance entry on the final finish so the WIP clearing account nets to
23	ZERO (the MAV zero-quantity-flush analogue for WIP) — manufacturing PUBLISHES, finance posts its own
24	entry (STRUCTURE §5), the costing-handler precedent.
25	
26	Postings per move type (the GL effect — D-020): the costing engine pre-selects the OFFSET and the
27	event carries it, so the stock-valuation handler is a thin Dr/Cr switch (RECEIPT/ADJUSTMENT-up: Dr
28	inventory / Cr offset; ISSUE: Dr offset / Cr inventory at the computed cost; the MAV zero-quantity
29	residual flushes to price-difference within the issue's entry; a reversal posts the exact reverse;
30	a value-neutral TRANSFER publishes no event). The detail lives in docs/modules/inventory.md.
31	
32	Journals are built through the finance posting service (``create_draft_entry`` + ``post_entry``),
33	NEVER raw inserts, so every invariant fires. The move's document is linked to the entry's document
34	('posts' edge). Registration: ``app.main.register_event_handlers`` subscribes the handlers at the
35	factory (the D-011 seam), so the test harness re-registers after its per-test reset (D-025).
36	"""
37	
38	from __future__ import annotations

76	# A signed posting (account_id, amount): positive => debit, negative => credit; the line builder
77	# drops zeros and splits into one-sided debit/credit lines.
78	_SignedPosting = tuple[uuid.UUID, Decimal]
79	
80	
81	async def post_stock_valuation_journal(session: AsyncSession, event: StockValued) -> None:
82	    """Post the COGS/inventory journal for a valued stock move (D-020), in the move's transaction.
83	
84	    Registered via ``app.main.register_event_handlers`` (the deterministic D-011 registration seam),
85	    not an import-time ``@on`` decorator, so the test harness can re-register it after its per-test
86	    ``clear_subscriptions`` reset (D-025) without relying on a module re-import.
87	
88	    Builds the signed postings for the move type, turns them into balanced one-sided journal lines,
89	    posts a COGS-typed entry dated the move date (the period trigger fires here — a closed period
90	    rolls the whole move back), and links move.document -> entry.document ('posts')."""
91	    currency_code = (
92	        await finance_queries.functional_currency_or_none(session, event.tenant_id)
93	        or DEFAULT_COSTING_CURRENCY
94	    )
95	    # total_cost is already quantized for ISSUE (per-layer / MAV quantize) but a RECEIPT's
96	    # qty × unit_cost can carry sub-currency digits — quantize the posted amount at the boundary
97	    # (D-015); the residual flush is already an exact MoneyType difference.
98	    amount = quantize_for_currency(Decimal(event.total_cost), currency_code)
99	    residual = Decimal(event.residual_to_price_difference)
100	
101	    postings = _postings_for(event, amount, residual)
102	    lines = _lines_from_postings(postings, event.item_id)
103	    if len(lines) < 2:
104	        # A zero-value move (e.g. a free receipt) produces no balanced entry — nothing to post. The
105	        # quant/valuation still updated; there is simply no GL effect. (Not reachable on priced
106	        # moves.)
107	        return
108	
109	    entry = await create_draft_entry(
110	        session,
111	        event.tenant_id,
112	        JournalEntryCreate(
113	            posting_date=date.fromisoformat(event.move_date),
114	            currency_code=currency_code,
115	            description=f"Stock {event.move_type.lower()} {event.move_number}",
116	            document_type=DocumentType.COGS,
117	            lines=lines,
118	        ),
119	    )
120	    await post_entry(session, event.tenant_id, entry.id)
121	    # Link the move's document to the journal entry's document so the docflow chain shows the COGS
122	    # posting (D-012 'posts' edge — the finance posting convention).
123	    await docflow.link_documents(
124	        session,
125	        event.tenant_id,
126	        predecessor=event.document_id,
127	        successor=entry.document_id,
128	        link_type=STOCK_MOVE_POSTS_LINK,
129	    )

132	def _postings_for(
133	    event: StockValued, amount: Decimal, residual: Decimal
134	) -> list[_SignedPosting]:
135	    """The signed GL postings (positive = debit, negative = credit) for the move (D-020).
136	
137	    The costing engine already chose ``offset_account_id`` per move type (ISSUE -> COGS; RECEIPT /
138	    ADJUSTMENT -> price-difference; a reversal -> the opposite of the original's offset), so the
139	    handler stays a thin Dr/Cr direction switch:
140	    - inbound: Dr inventory / Cr offset (stock entered or an issue was reversed).
141	    - outbound: Dr offset / Cr inventory (stock left or a receipt was reversed). The inventory leg
142	      additionally carries the moving-average zero-quantity residual, flushed to price-difference,
143	      so value and quantity reconcile to zero (D-020). ``residual`` is 0 unless the issue drove
144	      on-hand to exactly zero."""
145	    if event.is_inbound:
146	        return [
147	            (event.inventory_account_id, amount),
148	            (event.offset_account_id, -amount),
149	        ]
150	    return [
151	        (event.offset_account_id, amount),
152	        (event.inventory_account_id, -(amount + residual)),
153	        (event.price_difference_account_id, residual),
154	    ]
155	
156	
157	def _lines_from_postings(
158	    postings: list[_SignedPosting], item_id: uuid.UUID
159	) -> list[JournalLineCreate]:
160	    """Collapse signed postings per account, drop zeros, and emit one-sided journal lines (D-017):
161	    a positive net is a debit, a negative net a credit. The item dimension rides every line so the
162	    COGS entry is attributable to the item (D-017 dimensions)."""
163	    net: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = {}
164	    for account_id, signed in postings:
165	        net[account_id] = net.get(account_id, Decimal(0)) + signed
166	    lines: list[JournalLineCreate] = []
167	    for account_id, value in net.items():
168	        if value == 0:
169	            continue
170	        if value > 0:
171	            lines.append(
172	                JournalLineCreate(
173	                    account_id=account_id,
174	                    transaction_debit_amount=value,
175	                    item_id=item_id,
176	                )
177	            )
178	        else:
179	            lines.append(
180	                JournalLineCreate(
181	                    account_id=account_id,
182	                    transaction_credit_amount=-value,
183	                    item_id=item_id,
184	                )
185	            )
186	    return lines

188	
189	async def create_bill_for_match(session: AsyncSession, event: InvoiceMatched) -> None:
190	    """Create + post the AP vendor bill for a posted 3-way match (PLAN 6.4, D-042), in the match's
191	    transaction.
192	
193	    Builds a draft vendor bill whose lines DEBIT GR/IR at PO cost and route the in-tolerance price
194	    difference to the purchase-price-variance account, with the header tax code driving input tax,
195	    then posts it through the finance AP service (``create_vendor_bill`` + ``post_vendor_bill``) so
196	    every AP/journal invariant fires exactly as for a hand-entered bill. The AP control is credited
197	    at the vendor-invoiced gross, partner-keyed by the opaque vendor id (D-029); the bill's due date
198	    is invoice_date + the vendor's terms (procurement computed it). The GR/IR debit equals the GR/IR
199	    credit at receipt, so GR/IR nets to zero — the procure-to-pay loop closes. Linking the match
200	    document to the bill document ('billed_by') completes the PO → GR → match → bill docflow chain.
201	
202	    Registered via ``app.main.register_event_handlers`` (the deterministic D-011 seam), so the test
203	    harness re-registers it after its per-test ``clear_subscriptions`` reset (D-025)."""
204	    lines: list[VendorBillLineCreate] = []
205	    for line in event.lines:

207	        lines.append(

215	        # The price variance (taxable, same code so input tax matches the full invoice): Dr/Cr PPV.
216	        # Dropped when zero so a clean match posts no PPV line.
217	        if line.price_variance != 0:

226	
227	    bill = await create_vendor_bill(
228	        session,
229	        event.tenant_id,
230	        VendorBillCreate(
231	            partner_id=event.partner_id,
232	            partner_name=event.partner_name,
233	            bill_date=event.invoice_date,
234	            due_date=event.due_date,
235	            currency_code=event.currency_code,
236	            ap_account_id=event.ap_account_id,
237	            bill_external_ref=event.vendor_invoice_ref,
238	            description=f"3-way match {event.match_number}",
239	            lines=lines,
240	        ),
241	    )
242	    await post_vendor_bill(session, event.tenant_id, bill.id, posting_date=event.invoice_date)
243	    await docflow.link_documents(
244	        session,
245	        event.tenant_id,
246	        predecessor=event.document_id,
247	        successor=bill.document_id,
248	        link_type=INVOICE_MATCH_BILLED_BY_BILL_LINK,
249	    )

252	async def create_invoice_for_billing(session: AsyncSession, event: BillingInvoiced) -> None:
253	    """Create + post the AR customer invoice for a posted sales billing (PLAN 7.4, D-046), in the
254	    billing's transaction — the MIRROR of ``create_bill_for_match`` (match → AP bill), sign-flipped.
255	
256	    Builds a draft customer invoice whose lines CREDIT the sales-revenue account at each net (the
257	    header tax code drives output tax), then posts it through the finance AR service
258	    (``create_customer_invoice`` + ``post_customer_invoice``) so every AR/journal invariant fires
259	    exactly as for a hand-entered invoice: Dr AR control gross / Cr revenue net / Cr output tax,
260	    partner-keyed by the opaque customer id (D-029), due = billing_date + the terms sales computed.
261	    Linking the billing document to the invoice document ('invoiced_by_invoice') completes the

263	    journal trigger here and rolls the whole billing post back.
264	
265	    Registered via ``app.main.register_event_handlers`` (the deterministic D-011 seam), so the test
266	    harness re-registers it after its per-test ``clear_subscriptions`` reset (D-025)."""

268	        CustomerInvoiceLineCreate(

270	            description="Sales revenue",
271	            net_amount=line.net_amount,
272	            tax_code_id=line.tax_code_id,
273	        )

275	    ]
276	    invoice = await create_customer_invoice(
277	        session,
278	        event.tenant_id,

307	    (reversing AR), the header tax code reversing output tax — posted via

309	    document → 'credited_by' → credit-note document. A closed return period trips the journal

344	async def post_production_variance(session: AsyncSession, event: OrderFinished) -> None:
345	    """Post the WIP-variance entry for a finished production order (PLAN 8.2, D-048), in the
346	    finish's transaction — the MAV zero-quantity-flush analogue for WIP. The finished RECEIPT move
347	    credited WIP by the value entering stock; this posts the RESIDUAL WIP the receipt did NOT absorb
348	    so WIP nets to EXACTLY zero. ``variance_amount`` is SIGNED: positive = leftover DEBIT (cost
349	    overran → Dr variance / Cr WIP); negative = leftover CREDIT (under → Dr WIP / Cr variance); 0
350	    posts nothing. Manufacturing PUBLISHES; finance posts its OWN entry (STRUCTURE §5), as off
351	    StockValued. A closed period trips the trigger here and rolls the whole finish back. Registered
352	    via ``app.main.register_event_handlers`` (the D-011 seam)."""
353	    amount = Decimal(event.variance_amount)
354	    if amount == 0 or event.variance_account_id is None:
355	        return
356	    currency_code = event.currency_code or DEFAULT_COSTING_CURRENCY
357	    magnitude = quantize_for_currency(abs(amount), currency_code)
358	    if magnitude == 0:
359	        return
360	    if amount > 0:
361	        # Leftover DEBIT → Dr variance / Cr WIP (cost overran); leftover CREDIT → the reverse.
362	        postings: list[_SignedPosting] = [
363	            (event.variance_account_id, magnitude),
364	            (event.wip_account_id, -magnitude),
365	        ]
366	    else:
367	        postings = [
368	            (event.wip_account_id, magnitude),
369	            (event.variance_account_id, -magnitude),
370	        ]
371	    lines = _lines_from_postings(postings, event.item_id)
372	    entry = await create_draft_entry(
373	        session,
374	        event.tenant_id,
375	        JournalEntryCreate(
376	            posting_date=date.fromisoformat(event.move_date),
377	            currency_code=currency_code,
378	            description=f"WIP variance {event.order_number}",
379	            document_type=DocumentType.COGS,
380	            lines=lines,
381	        ),
382	    )
383	    await post_entry(session, event.tenant_id, entry.id)
384	    await docflow.link_documents(
385	        session,
386	        event.tenant_id,
387	        predecessor=event.document_id,
388	        successor=entry.document_id,
389	        link_type=PRODUCTION_ORDER_FINISHED_TO_MOVE_LINK,
390	    )

1	"""Domain events procurement PUBLISHES (D-011/D-041). Declarative data only — no logic, no models —
2	so inventory's ``handlers.py`` may import these typed classes (the STRUCTURE §5 events.py allowance:
3	an event carries no behaviour, so a subscriber in another module imports it without any logic).
4	
5	``GoodsReceiptPosted`` is the SANCTIONED cross-module mechanism for the goods-receipt → stock-move
6	effect (D-041). Procurement OWNS the GR document and its PO; it MUST NOT call inventory's service
7	directly (STRUCTURE §5 forbids importing another module's service). So the GR POST publishes this
8	event carrying everything inventory needs to create the stock RECEIPT moves — one
9	``GoodsReceiptMove`` per GR line (item, target bin, quantity, the snapshot unit cost, lot/serial,
10	the GR/IR
11	clearing offset account, the inspection flag) plus the move_date and the GR's core_documents id for
12	docflow linkage. Inventory's ``handlers.py`` subscribes, creates each move via its OWN service with
13	``valuation_offset_account_id`` = the GR/IR account (so the costing event credits GR/IR), and links
14	GR document → 'moved_by' → move document. The handler shares the session, so the moves + their
15	inventory-debit/GR-IR journals land in the SAME transaction as the GR post — all-or-nothing
16	(D-011/D-020): a closed period or any handler failure rolls the WHOLE GR post back.
17	
18	Procurement updates its OWN tables (the PO received_quantity, the GR status/posted_at) in that same
19	transaction AFTER publishing; it does NOT need the move ids back — the GR↔move link is the durable
20	docflow edge the handler writes, not a cross-module FK column (D-041).
21	"""
22	
23	import uuid
24	from datetime import date
25	from decimal import Decimal
26	from typing import ClassVar
27

29	
30	from app.core.events import DomainEvent

39	    stock RECEIPT move. Plain frozen data: the opaque item + target bin ids (D-029), the received
40	    quantity in the item's base UoM, the snapshot unit cost the stock enters at, optional lot/serial
41	    codes (created on the receipt for tracked items), and the v1 ``requires_inspection`` flag
42	    (passed through for traceability — Phase 9 adds the disposition; v1 does not block use)."""
43	
44	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
45	
46	    item_id: uuid.UUID
47	    bin_id: uuid.UUID
48	    quantity: Decimal
49	    unit_cost: Decimal
50	    lot_code: str | None = None
51	    serial_code: str | None = None
52	    requires_inspection: bool = False

55	class GoodsReceiptPosted(DomainEvent):
56	    """A goods receipt was posted (D-041). Inventory's ``handlers.py`` subscribes and creates one
57	    stock RECEIPT move per ``move`` in the SAME transaction, offsetting each to ``gr_ir_account_id``
58	    (Dr Inventory / Cr GR-IR), and links the GR document to each move document ('moved_by').
59	
60	    - ``goods_receipt_id`` + ``gr_number`` + ``document_id`` — the GR document (``document_id`` is
61	      the core_documents id the handler links the move documents to).
62	    - ``warehouse_id`` — the inventory warehouse the receipt's stock lands in (each move's bin is in
63	      it); carried for context / future per-warehouse routing.
64	    - ``move_date`` — the receipt date the stock moves post on (ISO date string); a date in a CLOSED
65	      period makes each move's valuation journal trip the period trigger, rolling the whole GR back.
66	    - ``gr_ir_account_id`` — the tenant's GR/IR clearing account (resolved by procurement from
67	      finance/queries before publishing); the valuation-offset OVERRIDE every move carries.

74	    document_id: uuid.UUID

76	    move_date: str

93	      unit_price), the basis the input tax is computed on for this line.

115	    - ``partner_id`` + ``partner_name`` — the vendor (the opaque finance partner_id, D-029) + name.
116	    - ``vendor_invoice_ref`` — the vendor's own invoice number, stored as the bill's external ref.
117	    - ``invoice_date`` + ``due_date`` — the bill's date + due date (procurement computes the due

120	    - ``gr_ir_account_id`` — the GR/IR clearing account the bill debits (resolved from finance by
121	      procurement before publishing).

123	    - ``ap_account_id`` — the AP control account the bill credits at the invoiced total.
124	    - ``tax_code_id`` — the opaque finance tax code (nullable) driving the input tax.
125	    - ``lines`` — the per-match-line bill postings (see ``InvoiceMatchBillLine``)."""

130	    match_number: str
131	    document_id: uuid.UUID
132	    partner_id: uuid.UUID
133	    partner_name: str
134	    vendor_invoice_ref: str | None

139	    ppv_account_id: uuid.UUID
140	    ap_account_id: uuid.UUID

1	"""The universal-journal posting engine (D-017): draft creation, two-flush posting, reversal.
2	
3	Every invariant lives at BOTH the service (here, for a clean 422) and the DB (migration 0009
4	triggers, the bypass-proof backstop). Three load-bearing mechanisms (D-017): (1) TWO-FLUSH
5	posting — the uow does not guarantee cross-table UPDATE order, so we flush the loaded lines'
6	``is_posted`` while the entry is still DRAFT (the line trigger keys on OLD.is_posted=FALSE),
7	THEN flush the header POSTED (balance + period triggers fire there); (2) LOADED-object mutation,
8	never bulk ``update()``, so audit diffs are captured and the audit bulk-write assertion holds
9	(D-010); (3) REVERSAL-only correction — a posted entry is never edited/deleted, only reversed.
10

12	balance check sums functional amounts, exact on both engines (MoneyType stores NUMERIC / micro-unit

60	    payload: JournalEntryCreate,
61	    *,
62	    functional_amounts: list[tuple[Decimal, Decimal]] | None = None,
63	) -> JournalEntry:
64	    """Create a DRAFT entry + lines (D-017). Validates: >= 2 lines, each one-sided, all accounts
65	    exist + postable + same tenant, and any cost-/profit-centre dimension exists in the tenant
66	    (PLAN 4.7, the service-level integrity replacing the absent FK on the trigger-bearing
67	    journal-lines table per D-022). Registers the document (no number; claimed at posting, D-012).
68	    Does NOT claim a number / resolve the period — both at posting.
69	
70	    Default: functional == transaction, balanced in TRANSACTION terms (the posting protocol then
71	    translates FX). With explicit ``functional_amounts`` ((debit, credit) per line; AP/AR clearing,
72	    D-019) those become the functional amounts and the balance check is on the FUNCTIONAL sums — a
73	    mixed-currency clearing entry balances only in functional, posted with skip_translation."""
74	    if len(payload.lines) < 2:
75	        raise ValidationFailedError(
76	            message="A journal entry needs at least two lines",
77	            code="finance.journal_too_few_lines",
78	        )
79	
80	    for index, line in enumerate(payload.lines, start=1):
81	        assert_line_one_sided(line, index)
82	    # Balance on transaction sides by default, on explicit functional sides for a (mixed-currency)
83	    # clearing entry where only functional must balance.
84	    sides = functional_amounts or [
85	        (ln.transaction_debit_amount, ln.transaction_credit_amount) for ln in payload.lines
86	    ]
87	    total_debit = sum((d for d, _c in sides), Decimal(0))
88	    total_credit = sum((c for _d, c in sides), Decimal(0))
89	    if total_debit != total_credit:
90	        raise ValidationFailedError(
91	            message="Journal entry debits and credits must balance",
92	            code="finance.journal_unbalanced",
93	            details={"total_debit": str(total_debit), "total_credit": str(total_credit)},
94	        )
95	
96	    account_ids = {line.account_id for line in payload.lines}
97	    await require_postable_accounts(session, tenant_id, account_ids)
98	    await require_dimensions(session, tenant_id, payload)
99	    entry_id = uuid.uuid4()
100	    document = await docflow.register_document(
101	        session,
102	        tenant_id,
103	        JOURNAL_ENTRY_DOC_TYPE,
104	        entry_id,
105	        doc_number=None,
106	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
107	    )
108	    entry = JournalEntry(
109	        id=entry_id,
110	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
111	        document_id=document.id,
112	        posting_date=payload.posting_date,
113	        currency_code=payload.currency_code,
114	        description=payload.description,
115	        document_type=DocumentType(payload.document_type).value,
116	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
117	    )
118	    session.add(entry)
119	    for index, line in enumerate(payload.lines, start=1):
120	        # ``sides`` is functional == transaction by default (posting translates FX), or the explicit
121	        # clearing functional amounts when supplied — either way one (debit, credit) per line.
122	        func_debit, func_credit = sides[index - 1]
123	        session.add(
124	            JournalLine(
125	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
126	                journal_entry_id=entry_id,
127	                line_number=index,
128	                account_id=line.account_id,
129	                description=line.description,
130	                transaction_debit_amount=line.transaction_debit_amount,
131	                transaction_credit_amount=line.transaction_credit_amount,
132	                functional_debit_amount=func_debit,
133	                functional_credit_amount=func_credit,
134	                currency_code=payload.currency_code,
135	                cost_center_id=line.cost_center_id,
136	                profit_center_id=line.profit_center_id,
137	                project_id=line.project_id,
138	                item_id=line.item_id,
139	                partner_type=line.partner_type,
140	                partner_id=line.partner_id,
141	            )
142	        )
143	    await session.flush()
144	    return entry
145

147	async def post_entry(
148	    session: AsyncSession,
149	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
150	    entry_id: uuid.UUID,
151	    *,
152	    rate_override: Decimal | None = None,
153	    skip_translation: bool = False,
154	) -> JournalEntry:
155	    """THE posting protocol (D-017 two-flush). Validates DRAFT + balanced, resolves + checks the
156	    open period from posting_date (422 before touching the DB), translates foreign-currency
157	    functional amounts (D-019; an explicit ``rate_override`` wins over the looked-up SPOT rate),
158	    claims the gapless number in this transaction, then flushes the loaded lines (still DRAFT) and
159	    finally the POSTED header (balance + period triggers fire there). Publishes JournalEntryPosted;
160	
161	    ``skip_translation`` (D-019, used by AP/AR clearing): the caller has ALREADY set each line's
162	    functional amounts (e.g. a payment clears its open items at the bill's frozen rate while the
163	    bank is at the payment rate, with a realized-FX line absorbing the difference). The engine then
164	    only validates those pre-computed functional amounts balance, never re-rating them — the one
165	    case where functional != transaction × a single entry rate.
166	    the caller commits via uow."""
167	    entry = await get_entry(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
168	    if entry.status != EntryStatus.DRAFT.value:
169	        raise ConflictError(
170	            message="Only a draft journal entry can be posted",
171	            code="finance.journal_not_draft",
172	            details={"status": entry.status},
173	        )
174	
175	    lines = await load_lines(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
176	    if len(lines) < 2:
177	        raise ValidationFailedError(
178	            message="A journal entry needs at least two lines",
179	            code="finance.journal_too_few_lines",
180	        )
181	
182	    # FX translation (D-019): recompute functional amounts at the posting rate when the entry is in
183	    # a foreign currency, balancing the functional residual into the largest line. After this the
184	    # functional sums (which the balance trigger checks) are exact and equal. Skipped when the
185	    # caller pre-computed functional amounts (AP/AR clearing realized FX) — the balance check below
186	    # then validates those.
187	    if not skip_translation:
188	        await translate_entry_lines(session, tenant_id, entry, lines, rate_override)
189	
190	    debit, credit = entry_totals(lines)
191	    if debit != credit or debit <= 0:
192	        raise ValidationFailedError(
193	            message="Journal entry debits and credits must balance and be positive",
194	            code="finance.journal_unbalanced",
195	            details={"total_debit": str(debit), "total_credit": str(credit)},
196	        )
197	
198	    # Period resolution + open check FIRST (service-level half of D-018); the trigger backstops.
199	    period = await queries.find_period_for_date(session, tenant_id, entry.posting_date)
200	    if period is None or period.status != PeriodStatus.OPEN.value:
201	        raise ValidationFailedError(
202	            message="The posting date is not within an open fiscal period",
203	            code="finance.period_closed",
204	            details={"posting_date": entry.posting_date.isoformat()},
205	        )
206	
207	    # Claim the gapless number in this transaction (D-012): gapless because the claim and the
208	    # POSTED commit succeed or roll back together.
209	    await ensure_sequence(
210	        session,
211	        tenant_id,
212	        JOURNAL_SEQUENCE_NAME,
213	        JOURNAL_NUMBER_PREFIX,
214	        JOURNAL_NUMBER_PADDING,
215	        year_reset=True,
216	    )
217	    entry_number = await claim_number(
218	        session, tenant_id, JOURNAL_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=entry.posting_date
219	    )
220	
221	    # Flush 1: denormalize onto the loaded lines while the entry is still DRAFT.
222	    for line in lines:
223	        line.is_posted = True
224	        line.posting_date = entry.posting_date
225	        line.fiscal_period_id = period.id
226	    await session.flush()
227	
228	    # Flush 2: promote the header. The period + balance triggers fire on this DRAFT->POSTED UPDATE.
229	    entry.entry_number = entry_number
230	    entry.fiscal_period_id = period.id
231	    entry.status = EntryStatus.POSTED.value
232	    entry.posted_at = datetime.now(UTC)
233	    await session.flush()
234	
235	    await docflow.set_document_status(
236	        session,
237	        tenant_id,
238	        entry.document_id,
239	        status=EntryStatus.POSTED.value,
240	        doc_number=entry_number,
241	    )
242	
243	    publish(
244	        session,
245	        JournalEntryPosted(
246	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
247	            entry_id=entry.id,
248	            entry_number=entry_number,
249	            document_type=entry.document_type,
250	            posting_date=entry.posting_date.isoformat(),
251	            currency_code=entry.currency_code,
252	            total_functional_amount=debit,
253	            account_ids=tuple(line.account_id for line in lines),
254	        ),
255	    )
256	    return entry
257

259	async def reverse_entry(
260	    session: AsyncSession,
261	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
262	    entry_id: uuid.UUID,
263	    reversal_date: date,
264	    description: str | None = None,
265	) -> JournalEntry:
266	    """Reverse a POSTED entry (D-017). Creates a NEW same-document_type entry with each line's
267	    debit/credit SWAPPED, posts it into ``reversal_date``'s open period (its own number), then
268	    sets the original REVERSED + reversed_by_entry_id — the ONLY mutation the immutability trigger
269	    permits. Links the two documents ('reverses'), publishes JournalEntryReversed, returns the
270	    reversing entry."""
271	    original = await get_entry(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
272	    if original.status != EntryStatus.POSTED.value:
273	        raise ConflictError(
274	            message="Only a posted journal entry can be reversed",
275	            code="finance.journal_not_posted",
276	            details={"status": original.status},
277	        )
278	    if original.reversed_by_entry_id is not None:
279	        raise ConflictError(
280	            message="This journal entry has already been reversed",
281	            code="finance.journal_already_reversed",
282	        )
283	
284	    original_lines = await load_lines(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
285	
286	    reversal_id = uuid.uuid4()
287	    reversal_document = await docflow.register_document(
288	        session,
289	        tenant_id,
290	        JOURNAL_ENTRY_DOC_TYPE,
291	        reversal_id,
292	        doc_number=None,
293	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
294	    )
295	    reversal = JournalEntry(
296	        id=reversal_id,
297	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
298	        document_id=reversal_document.id,
299	        posting_date=reversal_date,
300	        currency_code=original.currency_code,
301	        description=description
302	        or f"Reversal of {original.entry_number or original.id}",
303	        document_type=original.document_type,
304	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
305	        reverses_entry_id=original.id,
306	    )
307	    session.add(reversal)
308	    for line in original_lines:
309	        session.add(
310	            JournalLine(
311	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
312	                journal_entry_id=reversal_id,
313	                line_number=line.line_number,
314	                account_id=line.account_id,
315	                description=line.description,
316	                # Swap debit <-> credit in both currency pairs (frozen functional amounts).
317	                transaction_debit_amount=line.transaction_credit_amount,
318	                transaction_credit_amount=line.transaction_debit_amount,
319	                functional_debit_amount=line.functional_credit_amount,
320	                functional_credit_amount=line.functional_debit_amount,
321	                currency_code=line.currency_code,
322	                cost_center_id=line.cost_center_id,
323	                profit_center_id=line.profit_center_id,
324	                project_id=line.project_id,
325	                item_id=line.item_id,
326	                partner_type=line.partner_type,
327	                partner_id=line.partner_id,
328	            )
329	        )
330	    await session.flush()
331	
332	    # Post the reversing entry (claims its own number, runs the same period/balance checks).
333	    await post_entry(session, tenant_id, reversal_id)
334	
335	    # The single sanctioned mutation on a POSTED original (immutability trigger permits exactly
336	    # this: status POSTED->REVERSED with reversed_by_entry_id set).
337	    original.reversed_by_entry_id = reversal_id
338	    original.status = EntryStatus.REVERSED.value
339	    await session.flush()
340	
341	    await docflow.set_document_status(
342	        session, tenant_id, original.document_id, status=EntryStatus.REVERSED.value
343	    )
344	    await docflow.link_documents(
345	        session,
346	        tenant_id,
347	        predecessor=original.document_id,
348	        successor=reversal.document_id,
349	        link_type=_REVERSES_LINK,
350	    )
351	
352	    await session.refresh(reversal)
353	    publish(
354	        session,
355	        JournalEntryReversed(
356	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
357	            entry_id=original.id,
358	            reversal_entry_id=reversal.id,
359	            reversal_entry_number=reversal.entry_number or "",
360	            document_type=original.document_type,
361	            reversal_date=reversal_date.isoformat(),
362	        ),
363	    )
364	    return reversal

161	# (D-029: the open item is partner-keyed by the opaque vendor id on that line). A bill created
162	# DIRECTLY in finance (4.5) supplies its own ap_account_id per bill; the 3-way-match-triggered bill
163	# resolves it from this per-tenant posting default (procurement holds no AP account), so a tenant
164	# MUST map it before a match can post — resolved via finance/queries.ap_control_account.
165	AP_CONTROL = "ap_control"
166	
167	# --- AR control + sales revenue (PLAN 7.4, sales billing → AR, D-046) ---------
168	# The AR control (trade-receivables) account the billing-triggered customer invoice DEBITS at the
169	# invoiced total, and the SALES_REVENUE account each invoice line CREDITS at its net. A customer
170	# invoice created DIRECTLY in finance (4.6) supplies its own ar_account_id + per-line revenue
171	# account
172	# per invoice; the sales-billing-triggered invoice resolves them from these per-tenant posting
173	# defaults (sales holds no GL account), so a tenant MUST map both before a billing can post —
174	# resolved via finance/queries.ar_control_account + finance/queries.sales_revenue_account. The AR
175	# control mirrors AP_CONTROL; SALES_REVENUE mirrors the way PPV is a per-tenant default line
176	# account.
177	AR_CONTROL = "ar_control"
178	SALES_REVENUE = "sales_revenue"
179	
180	# --- WIP clearing + production variance (PLAN 8.2, manufacturing production orders, D-048) -----
181	# The WIP (work-in-process) clearing account is a per-tenant posting default (an ASSET/clearing
182	# account). A production order's component ISSUE posts Dr WIP / Cr Inventory and its finished
183	# RECEIPT posts Dr Inventory / Cr WIP, both via the inventory costing event's valuation-offset
184	# OVERRIDE to this account (the GR/IR-override pattern, 6.3). WIP nets to ZERO per fully-issued +
185	# finished order — the issue debits equal the finished credit plus any variance flush. A tenant
186	# MUST map this purpose before a production order can issue/finish (it has nowhere to clear WIP);
187	# resolved via finance/queries.wip_clearing_account.
188	WIP_CLEARING = "wip_clearing"
189	
190	# The production-variance account (an EXPENSE/income variance account) absorbs the residual when an
191	# order's accumulated WIP debit (issued component cost) differs from its finished-goods credit (the
192	# value entering stock at the WIP-per-unit cost × finished quantity) — over/under-absorption, the
193	# MAV zero-quantity flush analogue — so WIP still nets to ZERO at completion. The finish flow posts
194	# the variance as a separate entry (Dr/Cr WIP / Cr/Dr variance) AFTER the finished RECEIPT.
195	# Resolved via finance/queries.production_variance_account; a tenant MUST map it before an order
196	# whose finish carries a residual can complete.
197	PRODUCTION_VARIANCE = "production_variance"
198	
199	# Every known posting-default purpose: FX + the CO/bank/asset clearing accounts + GR-IR + PPV + AP +
200	# the AR control + sales-revenue defaults the 7.4 sales billing / credit-note flow resolves + the
201	# WIP clearing + production-variance defaults the 8.2 production-order flow resolves.
202	POSTING_PURPOSES: frozenset[str] = FX_POSTING_PURPOSES | frozenset(
203	    {
204	        CO_ALLOCATION_CLEARING,
205	        BANK_UNMATCHED_CLEARING,
206	        ASSET_ACQUISITION_CLEARING,
207	        GR_IR_CLEARING,
208	        PURCHASE_PRICE_VARIANCE,
209	        AP_CONTROL,
210	        AR_CONTROL,
211	        SALES_REVENUE,
212	        WIP_CLEARING,
213	        PRODUCTION_VARIANCE,
214	    }
215	)
216	
217	# Background-job registry keys (PLAN 4P.5/D-032, closes #26): long-running finance operations
218	# execute as jobs — their POST endpoints return 202 {job_id} for /api/v1/jobs polling.
219	FX_REVALUATION_JOB = "finance.fx_revaluation"
220	AP_PAYMENT_RUN_JOB = "finance.payment_run"

1	"""Purpose-keyed account wiring (D-019), split out of service/fx.py to keep both under the cap.
2	
3	A ``PostingDefault`` maps a purpose string (e.g. ``'fx_unrealized_gain'``) to a GL account, so any
4	flow that must post to a CONFIGURED account resolves it data-driven rather than hard-coding an
5	account code. The FX engine is the first consumer (gain/loss + revaluation adjustment); AP/AR and
6	inventory COGS reuse the same mechanism in later phases. Kept a distinct concern file (not in
7	fx.py) because it is account wiring, not FX rate math.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import uuid
13	
14	from sqlalchemy import select
15	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
16	
17	from app.core.exceptions import ValidationFailedError
18	from app.core.pagination import DEFAULT_LIMIT, OrderKey, SortDirection, paginate
19	from app.core.schemas import Page
20	from app.modules.finance.constants import POSTING_PURPOSES
21	from app.modules.finance.models import Account, PostingDefault
22	
23	
24	async def get_posting_default(
25	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, purpose: str
26	) -> uuid.UUID:
27	    """Resolve a purpose string to its mapped account id (D-019). Raises a clear 422 when the
28	    purpose is unmapped — a flow that must post to a configured account (FX gain/loss, revaluation
29	    adjustment) fails loud rather than guessing. The data-driven account wiring reused later by
30	    AP/AR and inventory COGS."""
31	    account_id = (
32	        await session.execute(
33	            select(PostingDefault.account_id).where(
34	                PostingDefault.tenant_id == tenant_id, PostingDefault.purpose == purpose
35	            )
36	        )
37	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
38	    if account_id is None:
39	        raise ValidationFailedError(
40	            message=f"No account is mapped for posting purpose '{purpose}'",
41	            code="finance.posting_default_unmapped",
42	            details={"purpose": purpose},
43	        )
44	    return account_id
45	
46	
47	async def set_posting_default(
48	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, purpose: str, account_id: uuid.UUID
49	) -> PostingDefault:
50	    """Map (or remap) a purpose to an account (D-019). Validates the purpose is a known FX purpose
51	    and the account exists in the tenant + is postable; upserts the (tenant, purpose) row.
52	    Loaded-object mutation on remap so audit captures the change."""
53	    if purpose not in POSTING_PURPOSES:
54	        raise ValidationFailedError(
55	            message=f"Unknown posting purpose '{purpose}'",
56	            code="finance.posting_default_unknown_purpose",
57	            details={"purpose": purpose},
58	        )
59	    account = (
60	        await session.execute(
61	            select(Account).where(Account.tenant_id == tenant_id, Account.id == account_id)
62	        )
63	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
64	    if account is None:
65	        raise ValidationFailedError(
66	            message="The mapped account does not exist in this tenant",
67	            code="finance.posting_default_account_not_found",
68	            details={"account_id": str(account_id)},
69	        )
70	    if not account.is_postable:
71	        raise ValidationFailedError(
72	            message="A posting default must map to a postable account",
73	            code="finance.posting_default_account_not_postable",
74	            details={"account_id": str(account_id)},
75	        )
76	    existing = (
77	        await session.execute(
78	            select(PostingDefault).where(
79	                PostingDefault.tenant_id == tenant_id, PostingDefault.purpose == purpose
80	            )
81	        )
82	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
83	    if existing is not None:
84	        existing.account_id = account_id
85	        await session.flush()
86	        return existing
87	    default = PostingDefault(tenant_id=tenant_id, purpose=purpose, account_id=account_id)
88	    session.add(default)
89	    await session.flush()
90	    return default
91	
92	
93	async def list_posting_defaults(
94	    session: AsyncSession,
95	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
96	    *,
97	    cursor: str | None = None,
98	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
99	) -> Page[PostingDefault]:
100	    """Keyset-paginated posting defaults, ordered by purpose (+ id tiebreaker; #27)."""
101	    stmt = select(PostingDefault).where(PostingDefault.tenant_id == tenant_id)
102	    return await paginate(
103	        session,
104	        stmt,
105	        order_by=[OrderKey(PostingDefault.purpose, SortDirection.ASC)],
106	        pk=PostingDefault.id,
107	        cursor=cursor,
108	        limit=limit,
109	    )

340	    journal lines carrying this ``cost_center_id`` in ``period_id`` of (functional debit minus
341	    functional credit). This is the amount ``run_allocation`` redistributes — CO is a projection of
342	    the journal (D-021), so the balance is derived from journal lines, never a stored total.
343	    MoneyType type propagation keeps the SUM exact on both engines (D-015); returns 0 when none."""
344	    debit = func.coalesce(

346	    )

349	    )

354	        JournalLine.is_posted.is_(True),

5	DEPARTMENTS, POSITIONS, and the reporting ORG CHART. Talent/recruiting/benefits and a

7	later 10.x plans (recorded in the parity doc and D-052).
8

10	employee's compensation/PII fields (``base_salary``, ``national_id``, ``tax_id``, ``date_of_birth``,
11	``bank_account``) are wrapped in ``Masked(tp, HR_EMPLOYEE_READ_COMPENSATION)``. A viewer WITHOUT the
12	``hr.employee.read_compensation`` key sees them serialized as ``None``; only the sensitive
13	permission
14	reveals the real values. Per the D-009 write-side convention, those masked fields are EXCLUDED from
15	the general Employee Update schema and are written only through a dedicated, permission-guarded
16	``PATCH /employees/{id}/compensation`` endpoint, so a partial update can never silently null
17	compensation.
18

20

22	  centre for labour-cost attribution — never finance models, never a cross-module FK.
23	- Links an employee to an OPAQUE core ``user_id`` (the login account; validated via a core user
24	  probe when set, never a hard FK from a module table to ``core_users``). An EMPLOYEE is a person
25	  who
26	  MAY also be a system user; not every employee has a login, and not every user is an employee.
27	- Publishes/subscribes to NO cross-module event in v1 (HR masters drive no cross-module effect;
28	  payroll in 10.4 will post a journal through the bus). So there is NO events.py / handlers.py here
29	  (an empty event file would be a dead file — STRUCTURE §8.3).
30	
31	The DEPARTMENT↔MANAGER circular reference (a department has a manager employee; an employee belongs
32	to a department) is resolved by making ``Department.manager_employee_id`` a PLAIN nullable
33	``sa.Uuid`` (opaque, validated in the service against ``hr_employees``) — NOT a hard composite FK —
34	so there is no circular composite-FK dependency between the two tables (D-052). The org-chart
35	reporting line (``Employee.manager_id``) and the department hierarchy (``Department.parent_id``) ARE
36	intra-table self composite FKs; the service guards both against cycles with a bounded walk-up.
37

39	one-directional (STRUCTURE §5 bans only bidirectional query imports). ``hr/queries.py`` is the only
40	file a later module (payroll, projects) would import.

12	- ``project_id`` is an OPAQUE projects-module id stored AS-IS and NOT validated in v1 — the projects
13	  module is Phase 11 (not yet built), so there is no table to validate against; the validation hook
14	  wires up when ``projects/queries`` exists (D-054). Do NOT create a forward dependency on projects.
15	
16	THE MAINTAINED TOTAL. ``Timesheet.total_hours`` is kept in step with the sum of its entry ``hours``
17	on every line add / update / remove (a denormalized running total, the stock-balance precedent) so
18	the header carries the period total without a per-read aggregate.
19	
20	The allocation REPORTING (set-based aggregates over APPROVED entries) lives in
21	``time_allocation.py``; reads + pagination live in ``time_reads.py``. ``from __future__ import
22	annotations`` keeps the model annotations strings at import.
23	"""
24	
25	from __future__ import annotations
26	
27	import uuid
28	from datetime import date
29	from decimal import Decimal
30	
31	from sqlalchemy import select
32	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
33	
34	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
35	from app.core.numbering import claim_number, ensure_sequence
36	from app.modules.finance import queries as finance_queries
37	from app.modules.hr import queries as hr_queries
38	from app.modules.hr.constants import (
39	    TIMESHEET_NUMBER_PADDING,
40	    TIMESHEET_NUMBER_PREFIX,
41	    TIMESHEET_SEQUENCE_NAME,
42	    TimesheetStatus,
43	)
44	from app.modules.hr.models import TimeEntry, Timesheet
45	from app.modules.hr.time_schemas import (
46	    TimeEntryCreate,
47	    TimeEntryUpdate,
48	    TimesheetCreate,
49	    TimesheetUpdate,
50	)
51	
52	# --- Loads + guards -----------------------------------------------------------
53	
54	
55	async def get_timesheet(
56	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, timesheet_id: uuid.UUID
57	) -> Timesheet:
58	    timesheet = await session.get(Timesheet, timesheet_id)
59	    if timesheet is None or timesheet.tenant_id != tenant_id:
60	        raise NotFoundError(message="Timesheet not found", code="hr.timesheet_not_found")
61	    return timesheet
62	
63	
64	async def get_time_entry(
65	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, entry_id: uuid.UUID
66	) -> TimeEntry:
67	    entry = await session.get(TimeEntry, entry_id)
68	    if entry is None or entry.tenant_id != tenant_id:
69	        raise NotFoundError(message="Time entry not found", code="hr.time_entry_not_found")
70	    return entry
71	
72	
73	def _require_draft(timesheet: Timesheet) -> None:
74	    """Lines are editable only while the header is a DRAFT (D-054)."""
75	    if TimesheetStatus(timesheet.status) != TimesheetStatus.DRAFT:
76	        raise ConflictError(
77	            message="Only a draft timesheet can be edited",
78	            code="hr.timesheet_not_draft",
79	            details={"status": timesheet.status},
80	        )
81	
82	
83	def _validate_period(period_start: date, period_end: date) -> None:
84	    if period_end < period_start:
85	        raise ValidationFailedError(
86	            message="The period end cannot be before the period start",
87	            code="hr.timesheet_period_invalid",
88	            details={"period_start": str(period_start), "period_end": str(period_end)},
89	        )
90	
91	
92	def _validate_entry_in_period(timesheet: Timesheet, entry_date: date, hours: Decimal) -> None:
93	    if not (timesheet.period_start <= entry_date <= timesheet.period_end):
94	        raise ValidationFailedError(
95	            message="The entry date must fall within the timesheet period",
96	            code="hr.time_entry_date_out_of_period",
97	            details={
98	                "entry_date": str(entry_date),
99	                "period_start": str(timesheet.period_start),
100	                "period_end": str(timesheet.period_end),
101	            },
102	        )
103	    if hours <= 0:
104	        raise ValidationFailedError(
105	            message="Time-entry hours must be greater than zero",
106	            code="hr.time_entry_hours_invalid",
107	            details={"hours": str(hours)},
108	        )
109	
110	
111	async def _validate_cost_center(
112	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, cost_center_id: uuid.UUID | None
113	) -> None:
114	    """A supplied cost-centre id must exist in finance (D-029) — VALIDATED via finance/queries (the
115	    department cost-centre precedent). ``project_id`` is deliberately NOT validated here: the
116	    projects module is Phase 11 (D-054)."""
117	    if cost_center_id is None:
118	        return
119	    if not await finance_queries.cost_center_exists(session, tenant_id, cost_center_id):
120	        raise ValidationFailedError(
121	            message="Referenced cost centre does not exist",
122	            code="hr.cost_center_not_found",
123	            details={"cost_center_id": str(cost_center_id)},
124	        )
125	
126	
127	# --- Timesheet header ---------------------------------------------------------
128	
129	
130	async def create_timesheet(
131	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: TimesheetCreate
132	) -> Timesheet:
133	    """Open a DRAFT timesheet for an employee over a period (D-054). Validates the employee exists
134	    and ``period_end >= period_start``; claims a gapless ``TS-`` number at creation. Rejects a
135	    duplicate (employee, period_start). No entries yet — ``total_hours`` starts at 0."""
136	    if not await hr_queries.employee_exists(session, tenant_id, payload.employee_id):
137	        raise ValidationFailedError(
138	            message="Referenced employee does not exist",
139	            code="hr.employee_not_found",
140	            details={"employee_id": str(payload.employee_id)},
141	        )
142	    _validate_period(payload.period_start, payload.period_end)
143	    if await _timesheet_for_period(session, tenant_id, payload.employee_id, payload.period_start):
144	        raise ConflictError(
145	            message="A timesheet for this employee and period already exists",
146	            code="hr.timesheet_period_conflict",
147	            details={
148	                "employee_id": str(payload.employee_id),
149	                "period_start": str(payload.period_start),
150	            },
151	        )
152	
153	    await ensure_sequence(
154	        session,
155	        tenant_id,
156	        TIMESHEET_SEQUENCE_NAME,
157	        TIMESHEET_NUMBER_PREFIX,
158	        TIMESHEET_NUMBER_PADDING,
159	        year_reset=True,
160	    )
161	    number = await claim_number(
162	        session, tenant_id, TIMESHEET_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=payload.period_start
163	    )
164	    timesheet = Timesheet(
165	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
166	        timesheet_number=number,
167	        employee_id=payload.employee_id,
168	        period_start=payload.period_start,
169	        period_end=payload.period_end,
170	        status=TimesheetStatus.DRAFT.value,
171	        total_hours=Decimal(0),
172	        notes=payload.notes,
173	    )
174	    session.add(timesheet)
175	    await session.flush()
176	    return timesheet
177	
178	
179	async def _timesheet_for_period(
180	    session: AsyncSession,
181	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
182	    employee_id: uuid.UUID,
183	    period_start: date,
184	) -> bool:
185	    """Whether a timesheet already exists for (employee, period_start) — the UNIQUE-guard probe."""
186	    stmt = select(Timesheet.id).where(
187	        Timesheet.tenant_id == tenant_id,
188	        Timesheet.employee_id == employee_id,
189	        Timesheet.period_start == period_start,
190	    )
191	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None
192	
193	
194	async def update_timesheet(
195	    session: AsyncSession,
196	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
197	    timesheet_id: uuid.UUID,
198	    payload: TimesheetUpdate,
199	) -> Timesheet:
200	    """Partial update of a DRAFT timesheet header (D-054). Only a draft is editable; ``employee_id``
201	    is immutable. A changed period is re-validated and must still contain every existing entry."""
202	    timesheet = await get_timesheet(session, tenant_id, timesheet_id)
203	    _require_draft(timesheet)
204	    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
205	    for field, value in data.items():
206	        setattr(timesheet, field, value)
207	    _validate_period(timesheet.period_start, timesheet.period_end)
208	    if "period_start" in data or "period_end" in data:
209	        await _assert_entries_within_period(session, tenant_id, timesheet)
210	    await session.flush()
211	    return timesheet
212	
213	
214	async def _assert_entries_within_period(
215	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, timesheet: Timesheet
216	) -> None:
217	    """A narrowed period must not orphan an existing entry's ``entry_date`` (D-054)."""
218	    entries = await hr_queries.time_entries_for_timesheet(session, tenant_id, timesheet.id)
219	    for entry in entries:
220	        if not (timesheet.period_start <= entry.entry_date <= timesheet.period_end):
221	            raise ValidationFailedError(
222	                message="An existing time entry falls outside the new period",
223	                code="hr.time_entry_date_out_of_period",
224	                details={
225	                    "entry_date": str(entry.entry_date),
226	                    "period_start": str(timesheet.period_start),
227	                    "period_end": str(timesheet.period_end),
228	                },
229	            )
230	
231	
232	# --- Time entries (DRAFT only; maintain total_hours) --------------------------
233	
234	
235	async def add_time_entry(
236	    session: AsyncSession,
237	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
238	    timesheet_id: uuid.UUID,
239	    payload: TimeEntryCreate,
240	) -> TimeEntry:
241	    """Add a time-entry line to a DRAFT timesheet (D-054). Validates the date is in the period,
242	    hours > 0, and the cost centre exists if set; ``project_id`` is stored AS-IS (NOT validated —
243	    projects is Phase 11). Raises the header ``total_hours`` by the entry hours."""
244	    timesheet = await get_timesheet(session, tenant_id, timesheet_id)
245	    _require_draft(timesheet)
246	    _validate_entry_in_period(timesheet, payload.entry_date, payload.hours)
247	    await _validate_cost_center(session, tenant_id, payload.cost_center_id)
248	    entry = TimeEntry(
249	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
250	        timesheet_id=timesheet_id,
251	        entry_date=payload.entry_date,
252	        hours=payload.hours,
253	        project_id=payload.project_id,
254	        cost_center_id=payload.cost_center_id,
255	        task_description=payload.task_description,
256	        is_billable=payload.is_billable,
257	    )
258	    session.add(entry)
259	    timesheet.total_hours += payload.hours
260	    await session.flush()
261	    return entry
262	
263	
264	async def update_time_entry(
265	    session: AsyncSession,
266	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
267	    timesheet_id: uuid.UUID,
268	    entry_id: uuid.UUID,
269	    payload: TimeEntryUpdate,
270	) -> TimeEntry:
271	    """Partial update of a time entry on a DRAFT timesheet (D-054). A changed date is re-validated
272	    against the period; a changed cost centre is re-validated; a changed hours adjusts the header
273	    ``total_hours`` by the delta."""
274	    timesheet = await get_timesheet(session, tenant_id, timesheet_id)
275	    _require_draft(timesheet)
276	    entry = await get_time_entry(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
277	    if entry.timesheet_id != timesheet_id:
278	        raise NotFoundError(
279	            message="Time entry does not belong to this timesheet",
280	            code="hr.time_entry_not_found",
281	        )
282	    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
283	    old_hours = entry.hours
284	    if "cost_center_id" in data:
285	        await _validate_cost_center(session, tenant_id, data["cost_center_id"])
286	    for field, value in data.items():
287	        setattr(entry, field, value)
288	    _validate_entry_in_period(timesheet, entry.entry_date, entry.hours)
289	    if entry.hours != old_hours:
290	        timesheet.total_hours += entry.hours - old_hours
291	    await session.flush()
292	    return entry
293	
294	
295	async def remove_time_entry(
296	    session: AsyncSession,
297	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
298	    timesheet_id: uuid.UUID,
299	    entry_id: uuid.UUID,
300	) -> None:
301	    """Delete a time entry from a DRAFT timesheet (D-054). Lowers the header ``total_hours`` by the
302	    removed entry's hours."""
303	    timesheet = await get_timesheet(session, tenant_id, timesheet_id)
304	    _require_draft(timesheet)
305	    entry = await get_time_entry(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
306	    if entry.timesheet_id != timesheet_id:
307	        raise NotFoundError(
308	            message="Time entry does not belong to this timesheet",
309	            code="hr.time_entry_not_found",
310	        )
311	    timesheet.total_hours -= entry.hours
312	    await session.delete(entry)
313	    await session.flush()
314

1	"""Timesheet approval lifecycle (PLAN 10.3, D-054): submit → approve / reject, and cancel
2	(reopen-to-draft).
3	
4	Split out of ``timesheets.py`` (header + entry CRUD) so each file stays under the 400-line cap
5	(STRUCTURE §8.4; the leave ``leave``/``leave_config``/``leave_accrual`` precedent). The header
6	lifecycle mirrors the leave-request submit → approve / reject precedent (D-053) but approves at the
7	HEADER level (the SAP CATS model) — APPROVED is the value-bearing state: only approved entries feed
8	the allocation aggregates in ``time_allocation.py``.
9	
10	``from __future__ import annotations`` keeps the model annotations strings at import.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import uuid
16	from datetime import UTC, datetime
17	
18	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
19	
20	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError
21	from app.modules.hr.constants import TimesheetStatus
22	from app.modules.hr.models import Timesheet
23	from app.modules.hr.service.timesheets import get_timesheet
24	
25	
26	async def submit_timesheet(
27	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, timesheet_id: uuid.UUID
28	) -> Timesheet:
29	    """Submit a DRAFT timesheet (D-054): DRAFT → SUBMITTED, awaiting an approver. Stamps
30	    ``submitted_at``. Re-submitting a non-draft is a conflict."""
31	    timesheet = await get_timesheet(session, tenant_id, timesheet_id)
32	    if TimesheetStatus(timesheet.status) != TimesheetStatus.DRAFT:
33	        raise ConflictError(
34	            message="Only a draft timesheet can be submitted",
35	            code="hr.timesheet_not_draft",
36	            details={"status": timesheet.status},
37	        )
38	    timesheet.status = TimesheetStatus.SUBMITTED.value
39	    timesheet.submitted_at = datetime.now(UTC)
40	    await session.flush()
41	    return timesheet
42	
43	
44	async def approve_timesheet(
45	    session: AsyncSession,
46	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
47	    timesheet_id: uuid.UUID,
48	    *,
49	    approved_by: uuid.UUID,
50	    notes: str | None = None,
51	) -> Timesheet:
52	    """Approve a SUBMITTED timesheet (D-054, the ``hr.timesheet.approve`` action): SUBMITTED →
53	    APPROVED. The value-bearing state — only APPROVED entries feed the allocation aggregates.
54	    Records the approver + approval time."""
55	    timesheet = await get_timesheet(session, tenant_id, timesheet_id)
56	    if TimesheetStatus(timesheet.status) != TimesheetStatus.SUBMITTED:
57	        raise ConflictError(
58	            message="Only a submitted timesheet can be approved",
59	            code="hr.timesheet_not_submitted",
60	            details={"status": timesheet.status},
61	        )
62	    timesheet.status = TimesheetStatus.APPROVED.value
63	    timesheet.approved_by = approved_by
64	    timesheet.approved_at = datetime.now(UTC)
65	    timesheet.notes = notes if notes is not None else timesheet.notes
66	    await session.flush()
67	    return timesheet
68	
69	
70	async def reject_timesheet(
71	    session: AsyncSession,
72	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
73	    timesheet_id: uuid.UUID,
74	    *,
75	    approved_by: uuid.UUID,
76	    notes: str | None = None,
77	) -> Timesheet:
78	    """Reject a SUBMITTED timesheet (D-054): SUBMITTED → REJECTED. Records the decider + decision
79	    time."""
80	    timesheet = await get_timesheet(session, tenant_id, timesheet_id)
81	    if TimesheetStatus(timesheet.status) != TimesheetStatus.SUBMITTED:
82	        raise ConflictError(
83	            message="Only a submitted timesheet can be rejected",
84	            code="hr.timesheet_not_submitted",
85	            details={"status": timesheet.status},
86	        )
87	    timesheet.status = TimesheetStatus.REJECTED.value
88	    timesheet.approved_by = approved_by
89	    timesheet.approved_at = datetime.now(UTC)
90	    timesheet.notes = notes if notes is not None else timesheet.notes
91	    await session.flush()
92	    return timesheet
93	
94	
95	async def cancel_timesheet(
96	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, timesheet_id: uuid.UUID
97	) -> Timesheet:
98	    """Cancel (reopen to DRAFT) a SUBMITTED timesheet (D-054): SUBMITTED → DRAFT, so the filer can
99	    edit and re-submit. A DRAFT is already editable (no-op conflict); an APPROVED / REJECTED
100	    timesheet is terminal and cannot be reopened."""
101	    timesheet = await get_timesheet(session, tenant_id, timesheet_id)
102	    status = TimesheetStatus(timesheet.status)
103	    if status != TimesheetStatus.SUBMITTED:
104	        raise ConflictError(
105	            message="Only a submitted timesheet can be reopened to draft",
106	            code="hr.timesheet_not_cancellable",
107	            details={"status": timesheet.status},
108	        )
109	    timesheet.status = TimesheetStatus.DRAFT.value
110	    timesheet.submitted_at = None
111	    await session.flush()
112	    return timesheet
113

1	"""HR HTTP layer (thin): parse -> call service -> return schema (PLAN 10.1).
2	
3	REST under ``/api/v1/hr``: departments (CRUD + filtered list with a conditional-GET ETag) here, with
4	the position surface (``position_router``) and the employee surface (``employee_router`` — the
5	masked
6	employee CRUD, the compensation endpoint, the org chart) mounted as sibling sub-routers at the foot
7	of this file so the whole module is ONE surface at ``/api/v1/hr`` (the maintenance order_router /
8	plan_router include precedent — no second mount in main.py). Every route is guarded by an hr
9	permission key (D-009); writes commit through ``run_in_uow`` (D-011) so audit rows ride the same
10	transaction. The department list is reference data, so it carries a conditional-GET ETag
11	(PERFORMANCE §3 / D-035).
12	"""
13	
14	import uuid
15	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
16	
17	from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request, Response
18	
19	from app.core.conditional import collection_etag, conditional_response, request_fingerprint
20	from app.core.deps import CurrentUserDep, SessionDep
21	from app.core.events import run_in_uow
22	from app.core.pagination import CursorParams, cursor_params, map_page
23	from app.core.rbac import require_permission
24	from app.core.schemas import Page
25	from app.modules.hr import service
26	from app.modules.hr.constants import HR_DEPARTMENT_MANAGE, HR_DEPARTMENT_READ
27	from app.modules.hr.employee_router import employee_router
28	from app.modules.hr.leave_router import leave_router
29	from app.modules.hr.models import Department
30	from app.modules.hr.position_router import position_router
31	from app.modules.hr.schemas import (
32	    DepartmentCreate,
33	    DepartmentFilter,
34	    DepartmentRead,
35	    DepartmentUpdate,
36	)
37	from app.modules.hr.timesheet_router import timesheet_router
38	
39	router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1/hr", tags=["hr"])
40	_CursorParamsDep = Depends(cursor_params)
41	
42	
43	async def _commit_read[T](
44	    session: SessionDep, work: Callable[[], Awaitable[object]]
45	) -> DepartmentRead:
46	    """Run a service call inside the D-011 uow and return the department refreshed + validated in
47	    the async context so a sync ``model_validate`` never trips MissingGreenlet (the maintenance
48	    _commit twin)."""
49	    holder: dict[str, DepartmentRead] = {}
50	
51	    async def _work() -> None:
52	        department = await work()
53	        await session.refresh(department)
54	        holder["read"] = DepartmentRead.model_validate(department)
55	
56	    await run_in_uow(session, _work)
57	    return holder["read"]
58	
59	
60	@router.post(
61	    "/departments",
62	    response_model=DepartmentRead,
63	    status_code=201,
64	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(HR_DEPARTMENT_MANAGE))],
65	)
66	async def create_department(
67	    payload: DepartmentCreate, current: CurrentUserDep, session: SessionDep
68	) -> DepartmentRead:
69	    return await _commit_read(
70	        session, lambda: service.create_department(session, current.tenant_id, payload)
71	    )
72	
73	
74	@router.get(
75	    "/departments",
76	    response_model=Page[DepartmentRead],
77	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(HR_DEPARTMENT_READ))],
78	)
79	async def list_departments(
80	    request: Request,
81	    response: Response,
82	    current: CurrentUserDep,
83	    session: SessionDep,
84	    params: CursorParams = _CursorParamsDep,
85	    is_active: bool | None = None,
86	    parent_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
87	) -> Page[DepartmentRead] | Response:
88	    """Conditional-GET supported (D-035): the is_active / parent filters fold into the fingerprint
89	    so a filtered 304 is correct."""
90	    fingerprint = request_fingerprint(params.cursor, params.limit, is_active, parent_id)
91	    etag = await collection_etag(session, Department, request_fingerprint=fingerprint)
92	
93	    async def builder() -> Page[DepartmentRead]:
94	        page = await service.list_departments(
95	            session,
96	            current.tenant_id,
97	            filters=DepartmentFilter(is_active=is_active, parent_id=parent_id),
98	            cursor=params.cursor,
99	            limit=params.limit,
100	        )
101	        return map_page(page, DepartmentRead)
102	
103	    return await conditional_response(request, response, etag, builder)
104	
105	
106	@router.get(
107	    "/departments/{department_id}",
108	    response_model=DepartmentRead,
109	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(HR_DEPARTMENT_READ))],
110	)
111	async def get_department(
112	    department_id: uuid.UUID, current: CurrentUserDep, session: SessionDep
113	) -> DepartmentRead:
114	    department = await service.get_department(session, current.tenant_id, department_id)
115	    return DepartmentRead.model_validate(department)
116	
117	
118	@router.patch(
119	    "/departments/{department_id}",
120	    response_model=DepartmentRead,
121	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(HR_DEPARTMENT_MANAGE))],
122	)
123	async def update_department(
124	    department_id: uuid.UUID,
125	    payload: DepartmentUpdate,
126	    current: CurrentUserDep,
127	    session: SessionDep,
128	) -> DepartmentRead:
129	    return await _commit_read(
130	        session,
131	        lambda: service.update_department(session, current.tenant_id, department_id, payload),
132	    )
133	
134	
135	# The position surface (positions + ETag list), the employee surface (masked employee CRUD, the
136	# compensation endpoint, the org chart), the leave surface (leave types + balances + accrual run +
137	# leave requests with the approval flow, PLAN 10.2) and the timesheet surface (timesheets + nested
138	# time entries + the submit/approve/reject/cancel flow + the allocation report, PLAN 10.3) are
139	# sibling sub-routers mounted here, so the whole module is ONE surface at /api/v1/hr.

2	
3	A sibling sub-router under the same ``/api/v1/hr`` prefix, mounted by ``router.include_router`` in
4	router.py (the leave-router precedent — ONE module surface at ``/api/v1/hr``, no second mount in
5	main.py). REST:
6	
7	- timesheets: CRUD + submit / approve / reject / cancel; a filtered, paginated list
8	  (employee / status / period range).
9	- nested time entries: ``GET/POST /timesheets/{id}/time-entries`` + ``DELETE
10	  /timesheets/{id}/time-entries/{entry_id}`` (a PATCH to update a line) — editable only while the
11	  timesheet is a DRAFT.
12	- allocation report: ``GET /timesheets/allocation?by=cost_center|project&from=&to=`` — APPROVED
13	  time hours grouped by the dimension over the entry-date range (the cost/project allocation
14	  deliverable).
15

17	are read by ``hr.timesheet.read``; create / edit-draft-entries / submit / cancel by
18	``hr.timesheet.manage``; approve / reject by the DISTINCT ``hr.timesheet.approve`` key. Writes
19	commit through ``run_in_uow`` (D-011) so audit rows ride the transaction; create / submit / approve

21	report is one GROUP-BY query.
